newsitem.title: USA: Rubin - Japan should seek domestic demand-led growth.
newsitem.headline: Rubin - Japan should seek domestic demand-led growth.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Sunday that Japan should seek to achieve domestic demand-led growth without increasing its current account surplus.

"It is very important for Japan, very important for the rest of the world that these objectives be met. We will all need to watch and see how this works out," Rubin told reporters, adding that this would be done in the period ahead.
Meeting with reporters following a gathering of the Group of Seven industrialized countries, Rubin also declined to go beyond an official communique on currency policies.
Rubin also said that he believed the outlook for the U.S. economy was one of solid growth with low inflation.
He told reporters that he did not see any reemergence of inflation, but conceded that it was important to be watchful.

Asked about the impact of the European Monetary Union, Rubin said he did not think it would affect the U.S. economy one way or the other, adding that he believed the dollar would continue to be the reserve currency.
Rubin said the G7 ministers seem to be somewhat more optimistic about the outlook for economic growth, but "that was tempered by a recognition of the many challenges we each still face."
While Rubin said that he did not see any indications at the present time of a resurgence of inflation, "one always has to be watchful in respect to inflation."
He added that, "It would not be my expectation based upon what I am seeing now that there would be a resurgence of inflation."
Asked about European monetary union, Rubin said, "We would not think that the effect on the U.S. economy would be particularly significant one way or the other."
"The bottom line," he continued, "is that we would expect the dollar to remain a reserve currency and the effects on the United States would not be particularly significant."
